# Implementation Plan: Full-Stack Todo Application

**Branch**: `001-fullstack-todo-app` | **Date**: 2026-03-13 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)
**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/001-fullstack-todo-app/spec.md`

**Note**: This plan was generated by the `/speckit.plan` command. See `.specify/templates/plan-template.md` for the execution workflow.

## Summary

Build a full-stack Todo application with a React 19 + TypeScript + Vite frontend and a Node.js/Express + SQLite backend. The app enables individual users to manage personal tasks through CRUD operations (create, read, toggle completion, delete) with a responsive UI, persistent server-side storage, and polished error handling. The frontend communicates with the backend via a RESTful API.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: TypeScript 5.x (frontend & backend), Node.js 20+ (runtime)  
**Primary Dependencies**: React 19, Vite 6, Express 4, better-sqlite3 (sync SQLite driver)  
**Storage**: SQLite (file-based via better-sqlite3, zero-config)  
**Testing**: Vitest + React Testing Library (frontend), Vitest (backend unit/integration)  
**Target Platform**: Modern evergreen browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge); Node.js server  
**Project Type**: Full-stack web application (SPA frontend + REST API backend)  
**Performance Goals**: Full todo list visible within 2s of page load; all actions reflected in UI within 1s (per SC-003, SC-004)  
**Constraints**: Responsive 320px–1920px viewports; WCAG 2.1 AA; no single JS chunk >200 KB gzipped; no offline mode  
**Scale/Scope**: Single-user, hundreds of todos max; one screen (todo list)

## Constitution Check

*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-check after Phase 1 design.*

| # | Principle | Status | Notes |
|---|-----------|--------|-------|
| I | Component-First Architecture | ✅ PASS | Plan decomposes UI into self-contained components (TodoList, TodoItem, TodoInput, EmptyState, LoadingSpinner, ErrorMessage). All live in `src/components/`. |
| II | Test-Driven Quality | ✅ PASS | Every component and API route will ship with behavioral tests. Vitest + RTL for frontend; Vitest for backend. `npm test` must pass before merge. |
| III | Accessibility by Default | ✅ PASS | Spec requires WCAG 2.1 AA (SC-007). Plan uses semantic HTML, `<label>`, keyboard navigation, 4.5:1 contrast. |
| IV | Performance & Responsiveness | ✅ PASS | Single-route app keeps bundle small. Responsive layout 320px–1920px (FR-012). Lazy loading not required (single route), but chunk size will be monitored. |
| V | Simplicity & Maintainability | ✅ PASS | Minimal dependencies (Express, better-sqlite3). No speculative abstractions. YAGNI enforced — no auth, no offline cache, no edit, no categories. |
| — | Technology Standards | ✅ PASS | React 19 functional components + hooks, Vite toolchain, Vitest + RTL, CSS Modules. No class components. |
| — | Development Workflow | ✅ PASS | Feature branch `001-fullstack-todo-app` from `main`. PR-based merge with constitution compliance review. |

**Gate Result**: ✅ ALL PASSED — proceed to Phase 0.

**Notes on Constitution Compliance**:
- The constitution describes a "client-side React application" but the spec requires a persistent backend. Adding Express + SQLite is a necessary extension. The constitution's principles (component-first, test-driven, accessible, performant, simple) all apply to the full-stack architecture. This is documented as a justified scope expansion, not a violation.
- The existing project uses `.jsx` files. The user explicitly requested TypeScript. Existing files will be migrated to `.tsx`/`.ts` as part of implementation.

**Structure Decision**: Full-stack monorepo with separate `backend/` directory and frontend at root (`src/`). The frontend stays in the existing Vite project root. The backend is a separate Node.js package under `backend/` with its own `package.json` and `tsconfig.json`. Root-level scripts orchestrate both (e.g., `npm run dev` starts both via concurrently).

## Constitution Check — Post-Design Re-evaluation

*Re-check after Phase 1 design artifacts are complete.*

| # | Principle | Status | Post-Design Notes |
|---|-----------|--------|-------------------|
| I | Component-First Architecture | ✅ PASS | Data model confirms single entity (Todo). Components mapped: App, TodoList, TodoItem, TodoInput, EmptyState, LoadingSpinner, ErrorMessage. Each is self-contained with own `.module.css` and `.test.tsx`. No monolithic render trees. |
| II | Test-Driven Quality | ✅ PASS | Research confirms: Vitest + RTL for frontend components, Vitest + supertest with in-memory SQLite for backend routes. Every component and route will ship with behavioral tests. |
| III | Accessibility by Default | ✅ PASS | Research resolved: `<ul>/<li>` for list, real `<input type="checkbox">` with `<label>`, `<button>` for delete, `aria-live="polite"` status region, visible form labels with `aria-describedby` for errors, 4.5:1 contrast for muted completed text (#767676 on white). |
| IV | Performance & Responsiveness | ✅ PASS | Single-route app — no code splitting needed. Mobile-first CSS with breakpoints at 768px and 1024px. Content constrained to ~640px max-width on desktop. Bundle will be well under 200 KB gzipped. |
| V | Simplicity & Maintainability | ✅ PASS | Research justified all dependency choices. Only 2 production backend deps (express, better-sqlite3). No ORM, no query builder, no state management library, no CSS-in-JS. Wait-for-server pattern chosen over optimistic UI for simplicity. |
| — | Technology Standards | ✅ PASS | React 19 functional components + hooks confirmed. Vite toolchain with proxy for dev. CSS Modules for styling. TypeScript throughout. No class components. |
| — | Development Workflow | ✅ PASS | Feature branch active. `concurrently` for dev. `npm test` gates both frontend and backend. |

**Post-Design Gate Result**: ✅ ALL PASSED — ready for Phase 2 task breakdown.

## Complexity Tracking

> No constitution violations require justification. The backend addition is a spec requirement, not a complexity violation — the constitution describes a "client-side React application" as the current state, not a constraint against server-side code. The full-stack approach is the simplest solution that satisfies persistence requirements (FR-007).
